skill.name: clojure-write
skill.description: Guide Metabase Clojure and ClojureScript work with style rules, REPL-driven development, linting, formatting, and test workflows.
skill.summary: Helps agents write, refactor, lint, and test Metabase Clojure code using project conventions.
skill.author: metabase

security_audit.summary: Static findings are mostly Markdown code spans and documented local Metabase developer commands, not Ruby backtick execution. I found no prompt injection, credential access, network exfiltration, or malicious persistence intent. One low-severity semantic issue remains because the lint workflow tells agents to commit changes without explicit user approval.

remediation.suggestion: Replace the commit instruction with guidance to present changes and wait for explicit user approval before committing.
State that REPL and mage commands should run only after user approval and only against the intended local project.

static_findings.snippet: When `clojure-mcp` tools are available (e.g., `clojure_eval`, `clojure_edit`), **always use them**
instead of shell commands like `./bin/mage -repl`. The MCP tools provide:
Only fall back to `./bin/mage` commands when clojure-mcp is not available.
This guide covers Clojure and ClojureScript coding conventions for Metabase. See also: `CLOJURE_STYL
- Acceptable abbreviations: `acc`, `i`, `pred`, `coll`, `n`, `s`, `k`, `f`
- Use `kebab-case` for all variables, functions, and constants
- Pure functions should be nouns describing the value they return (e.g., `age` not `calculate-age` o
- Functions with side effects must end with `!`
- Map destructuring should use kebab-case local bindings even if the map uses `snake_case` keys
- Every public var in `src` or `enterprise/backend/src` must have docstring
- Reference other vars with `[[other-var]]` not backticks
- `TODO` format: `;; TODO (Name M/D/YY) -- description`
- Make everything `^:private` unless it is used elsewhere
- Try to organize namespaces to avoid `declare` (put public functions near the end)
- No blank lines within definition forms (except pairwise `let`/`cond`)
- Prefer namespaced keywords for internal use: `:query-type/normal` not `:normal`
- Tag variables with `:arglists` metadata if they're functions but wouldn't otherwise have it
- Break large tests into separate `deftest` forms for logically separate test cases
- Test names should end in `-test` or `-test-<number>`
- Mark pure function tests `^:parallel`
- Follow `metabase.<module>.*` pattern
- Source in `src/metabase/<module>/`
- Follow `metabase-enterprise.<module>.*` pattern
- Source in `enterprise/backend/src/metabase_enterprise/<module>/`
- REST API endpoints go in `<module>.api` or `<module>.api.*` namespaces
- Put module public API in `<module>.core` using Potemkin imports
- Put Toucan models in `<module>.models.*`
- Put settings in `<module>.settings`
- Put schemas in `<module>.schema`
- Do not cheat module linters with `:clj-kondo/ignore [:metabase/modules]`
- All new endpoints must have response schemas (`:- <schema>` after route string)
- Request bodies use `snake_case`
- Routes use singular nouns (e.g., `/api/dashboard/:id`)
- `GET` endpoints should not have side effects (except analytics)
- `defendpoint` forms should be small wrappers around Toucan model code
- No raw MBQL introspection outside of `lib`, `lib-be`, or `query-processor` modules
- Application database uses `snake_case` identifiers
- Use `t2/select-one-fn` instead of fetching entire rows for one column
- New driver multimethods must be mentioned in `docs/developers-guide/driver-changelog.md`
- Driver implementations should pass `driver` argument to other driver multimethods
- Minimize logic inside `read-column-thunk` in JDBC-based drivers
- No `#_:clj-kondo/ignore` (keyword form)
- Use `:internal` `defsetting` instead
- **Lint PR:** `./bin/mage kondo-updated master` (or whatever target branch)
- **Lint File:** `./bin/mage kondo <file or files>`
- **Lint Changes:** `./bin/mage kondo-updated HEAD`
- **Format:** `./bin/mage cljfmt-files [path]`
- **Run a test:** `./bin/mage run-tests namespace/test-name`
- **Run all tests in a namespace:** `./bin/mage run-tests namespace`
- **Run all tests for a module:** `./bin/mage run-tests test/metabase/notification` Because the modu
Note: the `./bin/mage run-tests` command accepts multiple args, so you can pass
`./bin/mage run-tests namespace/test-name namespace/other-test namespace/third-test`
`./bin/mage run-tests test/metabase/module1 test/metabase/module2` to run 2 modules.
- **Check Code Readability:** `./bin/mage -check-readable <file> [line-number]`
> **Note:** If you have `clojure-mcp` tools available (check for tools like `clojure_eval`),
> **always prefer those over `./bin/mage -repl`**. The MCP tools provide better integration,
> richer feedback, and avoid shell escaping issues. Only use `./bin/mage -repl` as a fallback
- **Evaluating Clojure Code:** `./bin/mage -repl '<code>'`
- Send code to the metabase process REPL using: `./bin/mage -repl '(+ 1 1)'` where `(+ 1 1)` is your
- See `./bin/mage -repl -h` for more details.
To call `your.namespace/your-function` on `arg1` and `arg2`:
The `./bin/mage -repl` command returns three separate, independent outputs:
- `value`: The return value of the last expression (best for data structures)
- `stdout`: Any printed output from `println` etc. (best for messages)
- `stderr`: Any error messages (best for warnings and errors)
```bash
- Use `println` for human-readable messages
Feel free to copy these REPL session trials into actual test cases using `deftest` and `is`.

- Use Lib and MBQL 5 in new source code; avoid legacy MBQL

semantic_findings.title: Autonomous Commit Instruction
semantic_findings.description: The lint workflow instructs the agent to commit changes after fixing all issues. Marketplace skills should require explicit user approval before creating commits because commits change repository history.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The commit instruction is explicit in the lint workflow. Severity is low because it is local repository state, not credential access or network exfiltration.

content.value_statement: Metabase Clojure work requires strict style, testing, and REPL discipline. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through those project conventions.
actual_capabilities: Prefers clojure-mcp tools when available and uses mage commands only as a fallback.
Applies Metabase naming, docstring, visibility, formatting, and namespace conventions.
Guides REST API endpoint structure, schemas, parameter naming, and required tests.
Describes linting, formatting, readability checks, and targeted test commands.
Supports REPL-driven development with namespace loading and function evaluation guidance.
Covers Metabase-specific modules, MBQL, database models, drivers, and settings conventions.
limitations: It is tailored to the Metabase repository and may not match other Clojure projects.
It does not include executable scripts or standalone tooling.
REPL and mage workflows require a configured local Metabase development environment.
It gives coding guidance but does not guarantee correctness without tests and review.

use_cases.title: Contribute Clojure Changes
use_cases.description: A Metabase contributor can align new functions, namespaces, and docstrings with repository style before review.

use_cases.title: Refactor Existing Namespaces
use_cases.description: A maintainer can break large functions into smaller tested units while preserving module boundaries.

use_cases.title: Review API Work
use_cases.description: A reviewer can check endpoint naming, schemas, tests, and Toucan model placement against project rules.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Style Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Metabase Clojure code for naming, docstrings, visibility, formatting, and namespace conventions. Return only actionable findings.

prompt_templates.title: Guided Test Addition
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me add tests for this Clojure change. Start with the smallest failing test, then suggest the minimal implementation path.

prompt_templates.title: API Endpoint Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a new Metabase REST endpoint for this feature. Cover route naming, request and response schemas, side effects, and required tests.

prompt_templates.title: REPL-Driven Refactor
prompt_templates.prompt: Guide a REPL-driven refactor of this namespace. Identify small functions, evaluation steps, targeted tests, and readability checks before final edits.

output_examples.input: Review a helper namespace that exposes several public vars.
output: Marks internal helpers that should become private.
Suggests smaller functions where the logic is too long.

output_examples.input: Add a Metabase API endpoint for a dashboard action.
output: Checks route naming and side effects.

output_examples.input: Use a REPL workflow for a Clojure refactor.
output: Defines evaluation steps for each function.
Turns successful trials into focused tests.

best_practices: Use clojure-mcp tools when available, and ask before running shell-based fallbacks.
Add targeted tests before changing behavior, then run the smallest useful verification.
Keep Metabase conventions visible in reviews: schemas, docstrings, private vars, and module boundaries.
anti_patterns: Do not use broad lint suppressions to bypass module or style rules.
Do not evaluate broad or unrelated code in the REPL during a focused change.
Do not copy REPL experiments into source without tests and review.

faq.question: Does this skill run commands automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides workflow guidance. Command execution depends on the host agent, tool permissions, and user approval.

faq.question: Can I use it outside Metabase?
faq.answer: Partly. General Clojure advice transfers, but many rules are Metabase-specific.

faq.question: What tools does it prefer?
faq.answer: It prefers clojure-mcp tools when available, then documents local mage commands as a fallback.

faq.question: Does it cover ClojureScript?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill applies Metabase Clojure and ClojureScript conventions.

faq.question: Does it replace code review?
faq.answer: No. It helps prepare changes, but maintainers still need to review behavior, security, and tests.

faq.question: Does it handle credentials or deployment?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on local coding, linting, formatting, tests, and REPL workflows.
